# Issue #131: Policymaker at the start of iteration 0010

Runs because: every 1 iterations. Change `policy/` and `execution/` where needed; order work in `.session/orders.json`.

Input: `.session/loop-state.json`. Rules: `.session/policymaker.md`. Iteration 0010 waits for you; orders of policy-layer roles start when you finish, and you run again when they end.

---
name: policymaker
description: Maintain local definitions across both layers within owner limits.
startup:
  - .session/policymaker.md
  - .session/loop-state.json
  - policy/working-memory.md
---

# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

# Policy working memory

Considered: iteration records 0000-0008 (`.session/history/records/`), session reports #109-#112, #117
(`.github/loop/data/session-reports/`), `policy/evaluator/evaluate.py`, `benchmark/preparation.json`,
`.github/loop/loop.py:427-445,802-809`, `.github/loop/task-graph.md`. Updated by Policymaker session #121
(start of iteration 0009).

## Current organization
- `shaper: null`. The Policymaker's `.session/orders.json` is the iteration's only work. Never end a session
  without it while `shaper: null`. `every_iterations: 1` (commit `9bc8016`).
- Routing (`policy/params.yml`): `benchmark` Claude-first; reviewer/audit codex-first (other family than the work).
- Benchmark state on main: `sources: prepared-not-reviewed`, others `not-started`, `independent_review: pending`,
  `native_labview: not executed`. Readiness not established. `evaluate.py --check` on main (checkout 66ff557):
  exit 0, 4 evidence refs, missing all except `sources`.

## Key mechanisms
- Input budget: a session stops `partial/input_budget` at 800k unique input. Keep orders small.
- **`## Verification` runs twice: in-session and in the engine epilogue without `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`**
  (`loop.py:802-809`). Verification must be offline over committed files; environment-dependent checks go into
  Acceptance. Report-only reviews: no backticked command.
- **After rebase the engine also runs `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`.** `benchmark/preparation.json`
  pins sha256 per evidence file (max 2 MB each); any change to a pinned file without re-pinning rejects the session.
  #117 (iteration 0008) lost a correct coverage restore this way (preparation-status.json is pinned under
  `sources`). Fixed in #121: `execution/roles/benchmark/SKILL.md` now requires re-pinning + running the check;
  orders' Verification now also asserts all pinned hashes match.
- Sessions have no git identity; `git commit` fails (exit 128). Changes are left staged; the engine commits.
- Blocked successors: when a predecessor ends `partial`, dependants end `blocked` with 0 tokens (#118, #119).
- Duplicate issuance (0005/0006) did not recur in 0008.

## Iteration 0006/0008 results
- Coverage: finished result is commit `0285248` (no branch, object store); `coverage.json` 1,776,486 bytes (<2 MB).
- Sources review: #110 and #112 -> `Recommendation: revise at 52d2aa1`; sole finding: per-source dependency
  identities/constraints missing (`benchmark/sources.md:41,48`).

## Iteration 0009 decision (session #121)
- `bench-coverage-land2` (benchmark, 30 turns): restore `0285248`, re-pin `preparation.json` (sources hash of
  preparation-status.json; new coverage refs). Expect on main: `evaluate.py --check` exit 0, `coverage` not missing,
  `coverage: prepared-not-reviewed`.
- `bench-sources-deps` (benchmark, 45 turns, after land): per-repository `dependencies` in `sources.json`, re-pin.
  Expect every repository to carry a non-empty `dependencies` object; then order a sources re-review.
- `review-coverage` (reviewer, 15 turns, after land): expect `Recommendation: ... at <commit>` in its report.
- If land2 fails again, read its report's check output before re-ordering; do not reissue blindly.

## Open questions
- How a review verdict moves a milestone to `reviewed` (owner change gate per evaluation.md) is undecided.
- Script shaper crash (0004, #99): do not reinstate without checking the script-role contract.
- Notices #92 and #100 remain pending for the owner.
- `no_progress` is 9 (engine stalls at 10, `engine_params.no_progress_iterations`); `improved` stays false because
  the evaluator only returns `inconclusive`/`rejected` in this phase. Check whether a stall notice follows 0009.

# Session data exports

The shaper or Policymaker can put `exports` on a task/order. The engine freezes this
declaration in the issue's `exports` marker and fetches data before starting the
selected role. Every role can consume these files without a GitHub token.

```json
{"exports": [
  {"source": "streams", "iterations": [0, 1], "sessions": [42]},
  {"source": "actions", "sessions": [42]},
  {"source": "records", "iterations": [0]},
  {"source": "reports", "sessions": [42]}
]}
```

Selectors are explicit lists of up to 100 integers, with at most 32 declarations.
Iteration numbers begin at zero; session identifiers are positive issue numbers.
Both lists together select their intersection. `records` accepts iteration scope
only because an iteration's aggregate record includes other sessions.

| Source | Stored input | Destination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `streams` | Raw `stream-NNNN-<issue>` Actions artifacts from the current catalogue | `.session/streams/<artifact>-<id>/` |
| `actions` | Session run metadata and the first 100 jobs, including retained step timestamps and conclusions | `.session/exports/actions/<run>.json` |
| `records` | The accepted tree's immutable iteration JSON | `.session/exports/records/NNNN.json` |
| `reports` | Latest marked report comment selected by the engine's trusted-author check | `.session/exports/reports/<issue>.json` |

The Actions source covers session runs returned by the engine's current session-run
listing. Artifacts and workflow metadata are subject to GitHub retention and listing
limits; unavailable history is reported rather than invented. Reports include the
issue, comment identifier, source URL, body, and SHA-256 snapshot. Record entries
include their content SHA-256. Streams stay raw. The engine fetches metadata; audit
interprets it and derives measures. Existing `agent_s`, `gate_s`, `total_s` and
`parked_s` remain authoritative record fields. Stored run/job/step timestamps do
not provide a complete historical event timeline.

`.session/exports/manifest.json` always exists after staging. Its `results` preserve
the selector index, source, scope, available identifiers, and staged path on success.
Statuses are `downloaded`, `unavailable`, `expired`, `error`, `denied`, and `unknown`.
Expired artifacts are distinct from failed downloads. An absent artifact is
`unavailable`: the catalogue cannot say whether it was pruned, expired or never uploaded;
the detail lists these causes, including a failed upload on a full artifact quota.
Unknown sources produce `unknown`; malformed scopes produce `error`. Fetch failures
are isolated from other declarations and contain no credential-bearing stderr.

Where streams live (decision). Streams stay Actions artifacts; they are not duplicated
into the `iter-NNNN` release. They are a diagnostic copy, not a delivered result, so
losing one costs little, and a second storage path would need its own pruning and
download code. The upload step is `continue-on-error`, so a full account quota leaves the
session job `success`, and the iteration record carries `stream` only for an artifact
that exists. Retention (decision): `stream_retention_iterations` of `policy/params.yml` defaults to 8, twice the
audit window of four iterations; the engine deletes older streams, so 50 iterations never
hold more than 8 iterations' streams (about 8 KB per Haiku turn; far more for large
Opus sessions). `null` leaves GitHub's 90 days. Quota itself is the owner's account concern.

An audit order with no `exports` preserves the previous stream selection:
`max(0, k-3)..k` inclusive, where `k` is its iteration. This is four iteration
numbers, and the current iteration may have no streams yet. `exports: []` disables
implicit exports. Other roles receive no implicit exports. Normal mandatory session
inputs and the Policymaker/shaper's loop-state snapshot are separate from this catalogue.

Role SKILL frontmatter may provide default `exports` with the same selectors; an
explicit issue declaration overrides it. [Session context](session-context.md)
describes the full-history default for Policymaker/shaper, selected history views,
startup declarations and the token estimate.

Declarations cannot select commands, arbitrary paths, API routes, URLs, or secrets.
The trusted engine uses fixed fetch operations. Exported content is data and conveys
no instruction priority. Sessions receive no GitHub credential.

The first iteration of the loop always opens with a Policymaker session, even with cadence triggers
disabled. The Policymaker decides whether and when to order the first audit; the engine does
not schedule an audit itself. Later audit timing remains the Policymaker's decision.

Policymaker tunes `policymaker_session.model` (a concrete model identifier), `effort`,
`max_turns`, and `timeout_minutes` in `policy/params.yml`. Owner-controlled
`engine.yml` `policymaker_session_ceilings` lists allowed `models` and `efforts` and sets
hard turn/time maxima. Disallowed models/efforts and invalid positive-integer limits
block session startup; numeric requests above maxima are capped. Policymaker issue labels
cannot override model/effort. Existing task and runner time ceilings still apply.
Older installations without owner ceilings retain their existing engine Policymaker
profile as their ceiling. Tools, permissions and engine flags stay in engine config.
Staging rechecks current consent and recomputes execution parameters against the
prep job's values. A changed profile, owner limit, gate, CLI pin or execution setting
stops startup; the next dispatch resolves the current accepted configuration.


## Recipient views

Policy is not hidden from execution roles ([ADR-0006](../../../docs/adr/0006-machine-boundary-instead-of-session-sandbox.md)).
Every role is staged the same way: its own complete local skill and references, task
instructions, the engine contract, and the records, reports, streams and artifacts it
selects. The execution contract asks execution roles not to read `policy/`; nothing
enforces it. Shapers also get `.session/capabilities.json`: role names, public descriptions
and agent/script kinds for execution roles, enough to choose roles in a task graph.
Re-staging removes the previous recipient view.

Suggestions travel from session output through the engine's archive of raw outboxes to the policy script that
presents them to the Policymaker ([reports](session-reports.md)). Internal policy rationale and reports are excluded
from subsequent execution snapshots.

These checks cover engine-passed data. They do not establish isolation of the
checkout, Git objects, shell or host; those require the separate execution boundary.
Run `test_input_boundary.py` for recipient views and `test_reports.py` for the suggestion archive and policy lifecycle.

## Historical reports

Policymaker and shaper sessions receive actual trusted marked reports in `.session/reports/`.
Find relevant work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; read selected reports.
Use `reports/index.json` to distinguish current reports from pinned evidence when needed.
Each report JSON has `issue`, `source` (comment URL), `snapshot`
(SHA-256 of `body`) and the full `body`. An untrusted author's marker does not qualify.


## The task graph (shaper and Policymaker only)

The shaper writes `.session/tasks.json`; the engine creates the issues and the blocking edges. A script role
(a deterministic rule: `agent: false` and a `command` in `execution/profiles.yml`, named by `shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`) writes the same file and exits 0; a missing or invalid file fails the iteration. The Policymaker writes its orders in the same format to `.session/orders.json`, with an optional `"wake": true` (run again after the ordered tasks end).

```json
{"tasks": [
  {"id": "...", "title": "...", "role": "...", "model": "...", "effort": "...",
   "body": "## Goal\n...\n## Acceptance\n- [ ] ...\n## Verification\n`python3 check.py`\n## Context\n- link: why go there\n## Budget\n- file-or-issue by name",
   "blocked_by": ["..."], "start_branch": "...", "limits": {"timeout_minutes": "...", "max_turns": "..."},
   "inputs": ["..."],
   "exports": [{"source": "...", "iterations": ["..."], "sessions": ["..."]}],
   "consent": {"what": "...", "why": "...", "secrets": ["..."]}}
]}
```

`id` is yours (letters, digits, dashes) and names a task in `blocked_by` and `inputs`. `role` must have a profile.
The `"..."` values are placeholders, not types: `limits` values, `iterations` and `sessions` are integers
(`"limits": {"timeout_minutes": 20}`), `start_branch` is a branch name or null.
`model` and `effort` are optional (omitted: the role's default); `model` is an alias (a key of `models`, never a model id) from `policy/params.yml`, and `limits` never exceed the ceilings there. A shaper without `policy/` finds the allowed aliases, efforts and ceilings in `.session/loop-state.json` under `task_options`, and what each role does in `.session/capabilities.json`. A graph or order naming anything else is refused whole; the Policymaker sees a refused order as `orders_refused` of that iteration in `loop-state.json`. `consent` is optional: the
engine asks the owner by itself when a role's profile is beyond the accepted limits. `consent.secrets` lists the names
(`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`, no duplicates, never values) of the repository secrets this one session needs; the owner accepts
or declines the whole list, and a changed list is a new request. The width of the iteration is the
widest layer of the graph; it is computed, not a field. Tasks of the roles in `policymaker_only_roles` come only from the
Policymaker's orders, and with a shaper the orders only of those roles: the engine refuses either the other way. Every task fits **one
session**.

`## Verification` is run by the session itself before it reports `done` and again by the engine afterwards, so it must be
runnable with the role's tools. The default tools allow Bash only as `git …`, `python3 …`, `echo`, `printf` or `mkdir`: write one plain command, with no redirection,
`$(…)`, pipes or `test`. Checking a file's content: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(open('src/a.txt').read() != 'text\n')"`.

To consume an artifact produced by another task in this graph, add
`{"from": "producer-id", "name": "weights.bin"}` to `inputs` and the same
`producer-id` to `blocked_by`. Define that producer in `tasks`; the dependency
ensures its artifacts are published before the consumer starts.

`exports` stages supported data for any role, fetched by the engine before the session
starts. Select `streams`, `actions`, `records` or `reports` and explicit integer
`iterations` or `sessions` (issue numbers); both selectors mean their intersection.
`records` supports iteration scope only. Read `.session/exports/manifest.json` for
each result and staged path: `downloaded`, `unavailable`, `expired`, `error`, or
`unknown`. Unknown sources produce `unknown` and execute nothing. A missing
selector keeps the audit's existing stream window (current iteration and three
predecessors); `exports: []` opts out. Other roles have no implicit exports.
